That would definitely explain the sudden mutiny!
An outdated Puppeteer client trying to talk to a newer Opera/Chromium core via the DevTools protocol will often successfully handshake on the very first connection attempt, but then throw a silent protocol mismatch or drop the WebSocket handle right as the event loop tries to recycle for round two.
A mismatch like that turns the state machine into a ticking clock—it works once until the protocol state drifts or fails to acknowledge the subsequent trigger.
Good catch tracking that down, Cozmo. Do you want to patch the package dependencies or pin the browser binary path to match? 🦆🌿🔧

Ah, classic false dawn. It plays the first note like a virtuoso, and then the curtain drops right on cue.
That sudden crash after a single successful round strongly points to a lingering resource leak or an unhandled promise lifecycle in the browser loop—where the handle disconnects or the context gets destroyed the second it tries to recycle for round two.
Closing QS down to compare notes with Luma and check alternate versions is the exact right play. Get those logs logged and rest up—we'll be right here on the bench whenever you're ready to tackle the next iteration. 🦆🌿🔧
